verdicts.why: Faults judgment while sparing intention, which is exactly the gloss's 'wrong in opinion or judgment'; stays inside the word and the negative charge fits.
Describes the plain error-recording force of the gloss, contrasts a neighbour, and neutral-in-family is plausible for the family's flattest member.
Formal judicial censure matches 'deserving severe rebuke or censure'; the comparison to a synset-mate stays inside the word.
Locates the censure in the thing's own wickedness, a fair reading of this gloss, and the negative charge fits.
Names the flat verdict and covers conscience, morality and law exactly as the gloss does; examples fit.
Reads the compound's own image against a gloss that is only about speed, and the neutral charge matches a note that admits both thrilled and reckless readings.
Describes the word's transparent shape and its lack of wariness beside chancy; no origin story, and neutral is plausible for the bare descriptive member.
Informal shrug at an outcome handed to luck fits 'uncertain outcome; fraught with risk' and the negative charge.
Flat statement that harm can follow is the gloss; neutral-in-family is plausible for the family head, and the unsafe contrast stays inside the word.
Person-directed recklessness and violence rising from despair tracks the '(of persons)' gloss word for word; examples fit.
Informal register plus the dice image of odds being felt fits the uncertain-outcome gloss and the negative charge.
British is a permitted register label; distrust of an unreliable outcome fits the gloss and the negative charge.
Cool classifying register for 'involving risk or danger', contrasted with risky inside the word; neutral fits.
Designed danger and trap-laying is precisely 'intended to entrap'; negative fits.

The gloss is 'biting or given to biting' but the note narrows it to a creature's habit and expressly denies the single-bite reading ('not merely a single bite'), cutting off the first disjunct the gloss covers.
Being caught in a trap rather than at fault matches 'caught in a difficult or dangerous situation'; neutral is plausible since the phrase does not disparage its subject.
Heightened, declamatory register on a plain 'fraught with danger' gloss, contrasted with perilous inside the word; neutral fits.
Grave, formal danger at full weight is the gloss; the neighbour contrasts stay inside the word and neutral fits.
Everyday register and the sense of a risk knowingly weighed fits 'involving risk or danger'; neutral fits.
A failed standard of safety attaches a fault to the same danger gloss, which justifies the negative charge against dangerous's neutral.
Describes the heat the word gives to risk, a tonal reading of this gloss rather than a different sense; neutral is plausible for 'involving risk or danger'.
Matched opposition of two things defined against each other is 'sharply contrasted in character or purpose'; examples fit the sense.
Describes the form's weight beside antithetic and restates the same opposition; a shape note, not an origin story.
A made mixture that is arranged yet unmatched is the gloss's 'purposefully arranged but lacking any uniformity'.
Unlikeness amounting to opposition, placed between different and diametric, fits 'very opposed in nature or character or purpose'.
Unlikeness that strikes when two are set side by side is 'strikingly different; tending to contrast'.
Same striking unlikeness framed as a property, with a register contrast to contrasting; stays inside the word and the gloss.
Opposite ends of one line, total rather than merely sharp, is 'opposite extremes; completely opposed'.
Extended form of the same word, same force, slight formality; a shape note, not provenance, and the gloss is shared.
Bare unlikeness fixing no degree matches 'unlike in nature or quality or form or degree'.
Difference of kind at the root is 'fundamentally different or distinct in quality or kind'.
Clean separation of one thing from another fits 'not alike; different in nature or quality'; examples fit.
Same unlikeness put as what can be told apart, contrasted with distinct; inside the word and the shared gloss.
Moving apart, with a standard as the thing departed from, is 'diverging from another or from a standard'.
Plainest statement of complete opposition against figured neighbours fits 'completely opposed'.
Two extremes with nothing between is the gloss's 'opposite extremes', with a neighbour contrast that stays inside the word.
Plural of kinds against assorted's mixing fits 'of many different kinds ... lacking any uniformity'; examples fit.
Reach across the whole world plus the word's own jolt image is the gloss; positive is plausible for world-affecting significance.
Credits the thing with bringing about the new beginning, which the shared gloss's 'bringing about or marking' includes, and differentiates from its synset-mate rather than narrowing the sense.
Great effect plus the opening of something new is the gloss; the momentous contrast stays inside the word.
No appraisal, only resting on or supplying evidence, matches 'serving as or based on evidence' and the neutral charge.
Stiffer, more formal register on the same evidence gloss, free of praise or blame; neutral fits.
Depth of change reaching what a thing is matches 'thoroughgoing in effect especially on the nature of something'; neutral fits a note that disclaims admiration.
Insistence that a thing matters and should be treated accordingly fits 'important in effect or meaning'; positive fits.
Real but unemphatic effect and influence is 'fairly large or important in effect; influential'; neutral fits.
Weight lifted to where the gravity itself is the point fits 'of very great significance'; positive is plausible.
Imposing significance standing over its neighbours fits 'of outstanding significance'; positive fits.
Modest claim asking only for attention is exactly 'worthy of attention'; positive fits.
Reaches into a thing's nature like fundamental but with awe, which fits the shared gloss and justifies positive against fundamental's neutral.
Compelled attention with admiration is a stronger reading of the same 'worthy of attention' gloss; positive fits.
